Messages.Author: Cartman
Messages.Body:
Can I use the maneuver granted by a weapon used by a Ghoul Retainer I'm
equipped with?

Thanx

Messages.Author: Flux
Messages.Body:
"Cartman" <federi...@libero.it> wrote in
news:mtZ28.22891$ly.7...@twister1.libero.it:

> Can I use the maneuver granted by a weapon used by a Ghoul Retainer I'm
> equipped with?

For a minion to use the maneuver from a weapon he has to strike with that
weapon, preventing the Ghoul Retainer from using that weapon. You can't
use the maneuver from two different weapons either since then you'd have
to strike with both in one strike, which is impossible.

Short answer: No. :-)

Flux

it's different from your employing minion strike, yes.

Yes.

> during an Immortal grapple? Heck even with a Drawn out Beast.

yes and yes. Isn't that nice ? =)

> And
> the ghoul will still fire even if his controller was sent to torpor

Nope. the ghoul and the employing vampire "share" the same strike
resolution. If you strike with first strike, so does your ghoul. If you are
hit with first strike and send to torpor, your ghoul won't hit your opponent
either.

> Plus the hit can't be stopped by most fortitude
> cards, those that only effect stikes.

Skin of Rock, Flesh of marble, Hidden strength, Resilience, Apparition (...)
will still hose your ghoul strike easily.

> He does cost 2 pool, and he's
> unique

no, a ghoul retainer is not unique. you can have multiples in play, even
many on the same vampire.

> but still it seems like he's getting better and better. Heck
> he's more fearsome in combat than most vampires!

Let's say your opponent faces multiple opponents instead of only one. ;)

reyda

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Reyda wrote:
> "Matt" <mathi...@hotmail.com> wrote in message

> > And
> > the ghoul will still fire even if his controller was sent to torpor
> > with first strike?
>
> Nope. the ghoul and the employing vampire "share" the same strike
> resolution. If you strike with first strike, so does your ghoul. If you are
> hit with first strike and send to torpor, your ghoul won't hit your opponent
> either.

Not quite. The Ghoul uses the weapon during the normal (non-First Strike)
strike resolution, regardless of what his employer does. If the employer
goes to torpor from the opponent's First Strike strike, then combat ends
before the Ghoul can do anything, as you say, though.
